statement: A farmer says: "Not all of my 6 sheep are white." She is telling the truth. Which of these must be true?

choices.text: None of her sheep is white.
choices.misconception: I thought "not all are white" means the same as "none are white".

choices.text: At least one of her sheep is not white.
Exactly one of her sheep is not white.
choices.misconception: I thought "not all" means "all but one", but more than one sheep could be another colour.

choices.text: At least one of her sheep is white.
choices.misconception: I thought some sheep must still be white, but all six could be another colour.

choices.text: Most of her sheep are white.
choices.misconception: I pictured a flock that is mostly white, but the farmer did not say how many are white.

hints: What would make the farmer's sentence false?
"Not all are white" is false only when every single sheep is white. So for it to be true, there must be at least one sheep that breaks the pattern. Check each choice against that.
If all 6 were white, she would be lying. So at least one sheep is not white, and that is all you know.

solutions.reliable: The statement "not all of my sheep are white" would be false only if all 6 were white. Since it is true, at least one sheep is not white. Nothing else is fixed: she could have one, three or even all six sheep that are not white. So only "at least one is not white" must be true. The transferable idea: "not all" means "at least one is not", nothing more.

whyOnTest: Kangaroo checks whether you read "not all" precisely, and each wrong choice reads more into it than it says.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
